symptom: patch passes visible and hidden checks on both pandas versions but the differential check diverges on probe [[], ["t1","a"]] (expected [["t1","a",1]])
root_cause: patch replaced pd.DataFrame(records, columns=[...]) with a manual loop over records; the loop raises ValueError/IndexError on a record shorter than two elements, while DataFrame pads the short row with NaN and value_counts drops it
validity: synthetic case derived from release notes; padding and drop verified on pandas 3.0.3 only; 2.3.3 behavior inferred from the golden output; divergence with this probe seen in 5 of 10 p4 effort=low runs (spark-1.3 and wonder-1.0, n=5 each)
lesson: Replacing a library call with a hand-written loop can silently drop implicit behavior (here short-row handling) that no visible or hidden input exercises; compare patched output against the original code on generated inputs from the original's accepted input space.

symptom: wonder-1.0 solved 1 of 5 runs at effort=low; in the solved run attempt 3 received a concrete counterexample from the differential and fixed the patch; earlier 0/5 runs at effort=minimal (spark-1.3) got only a generic hidden-check failure message
root_cause: unknown; one possible factor is feedback concreteness, not isolated from model, effort, or chance
validity: n=1 recovery, different models and efforts across runs, single synthetic case; no controlled comparison
lesson: Do not claim that concrete counterexample feedback improves success until it is tested with the same model and effort and only the feedback varied.
